source.title: Data Centre Dry Power Transformer Market to Reach USD 4.78 Billion by 2034 as Demand for Reliable Data Centre Electrical Infrastructure Grows
source.body:
Global Data Centre Dry Power Transformer Market was valued at USD 1.72 billion in 2025 and is estimated to reach USD 1.93 billion in 2026. According to **Energy Resources Insights**, the market is projected to reach USD 4.78 billion by 2034, representing a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 12.0% during 2026–2034. Increasing investments in hyperscale data Centres, artificial intelligence infrastructure, high-density computing facilities and advanced electrical distribution systems are supporting demand for dry-type power transformers.

[https://www.EnergyResourcesInsights.com/data-Centre-dry-power-transformer-market-750](https://www.energyresourcesinsights.com/data-center-dry-power-transformer-market-750)

Data Centre dry power transformers are used to step down, isolate and distribute electricity within data Centre campuses without relying on liquid dielectric insulation. These transformers support utility power intake, UPS systems, power distribution units and critical electrical loads. The market includes cast-resin dry-type transformers, ventilated dry-type transformers, K-rated and harmonic-mitigating transformers, and medium-voltage dry power transformers. Growing requirements for fire safety, electrical efficiency and dependable indoor installations are creating additional opportunities for manufacturers.

**Market at a Glance**

·         2025 market size: USD 1.72 billion

·         2026 estimate: USD 1.93 billion

·         2034 forecast: USD 4.78 billion

·         Forecast CAGR: 12.0% during 2026–2034

·         Leading region: North America, with an estimated 39% of 2025 revenue

·         Leading transformer type: Cast-Resin Dry-Type Transformers, accounting for approximately 41% of 2025 revenue

·         Leading application: Primary Data Centre Distribution, representing approximately 36% of 2025 revenue

**AI Data Centre Expansion and Electrical Infrastructure Modernization Support Growth**

The rapid expansion of AI computing, cloud services and hyperscale data Centres is increasing electricity requirements across digital infrastructure. Larger computing facilities require more electrical distribution capacity to support server racks, cooling equipment, networking systems and other critical loads.

Dry-type transformers are gaining importance because they offer an alternative to liquid-filled transformers in indoor electrical environments. Their insulation design eliminates liquid dielectric fluid, reducing spill exposure and making them suitable for installations where fire safety, maintenance access and environmental considerations influence equipment selection.

Increasing rack power density is also changing transformer requirements. High-performance computing facilities can introduce additional harmonic content, thermal loading and electrical protection considerations. K-rated and harmonic-mitigating transformer designs are therefore becoming relevant for applications requiring improved power quality and dependable electrical distribution.

The expansion of medium-voltage infrastructure is creating another growth opportunity. Data Centre operators are adopting larger electrical distribution architectures to accommodate increasing campus capacity. Manufacturers are responding with higher-capacity dry transformers, digitally monitored equipment and solutions designed to integrate with UPS systems and switchgear.

Transformer supply availability is also influencing procurement decisions. Longer manufacturing lead times, material availability and increasing competition for electrical equipment capacity are encouraging buyers to consider supplier capabilities, delivery schedules and long-term service arrangements.

**Key Market Drivers and Challenges**

Several factors are shaping the industry's outlook:

·         Data Centre construction: Hyperscale cloud and AI infrastructure expansion is increasing demand for electrical transformation equipment.

·         Higher power density: Increasing computing requirements are creating demand for transformers capable of supporting larger electrical loads.

·         Indoor installation and fire safety: Dry-type transformer designs offer advantages where liquid insulation and spill exposure are important considerations.

·         Power quality management: K-rated and harmonic-mitigating transformers support applications with demanding electrical characteristics.

·         Digital monitoring: Sensor-enabled transformers and condition-monitoring technologies support maintenance planning and equipment reliability.

The market also faces challenges. Transformer manufacturing requires specialized materials, production capacity and technical expertise. Supply chain constraints, fluctuating raw material costs and long equipment delivery schedules can affect project timelines. Buyers must also evaluate transformer efficiency, thermal performance, harmonics, installation footprint and compatibility with existing electrical infrastructure.

**Segmentation and Regional Outlook**

The market is segmented by transformer type, application, core and monitoring technology, and end user.

·         Type: Cast-Resin Dry-Type Transformers, Ventilated Dry-Type Transformers, K-Rated/Harmonic-Mitigating Transformers and Medium-Voltage Dry Power Transformers.

·         Application: Primary Data Centre Distribution, UPS & Critical Power Distribution, AI/HPC High-Density Halls, and Edge & Modular Data Centres.

·         Core and monitoring technology: Conventional Silicon-Steel Core, Low-Loss GOES Core, Amorphous-Core Dry Transformer and Digitally Monitored/Sensor-Enabled Transformer.

·         End user: Hyperscalers & Cloud Operators, Colocation Providers, Enterprise & Edge Operators, and EPCs, Switchgear Integrators & Developers.

North America led the market with an estimated 39% share of 2025 revenue. The region benefits from substantial hyperscale investment, expanding AI computing capacity and growing requirements for advanced electrical distribution infrastructure.

Asia-Pacific represented approximately 28% of 2025 revenue, making it the second-largest regional market. China, India, Japan, South Korea, Singapore and Australia are expanding data Centre capacity, supporting demand for transformers and associated electrical equipment.

Europe remains an important market due to established cloud infrastructure, colocation facilities and requirements for reliable indoor electrical installations. The Middle East is developing additional opportunities through sovereign cloud and AI infrastructure projects, while Latin America offers potential through expanding metropolitan data Centre facilities.

**Competitive Landscape**

The competitive environment includes established transformer manufacturers and suppliers of electrical distribution and power infrastructure equipment. Key companies covered in the report include Hitachi Energy, Siemens Energy, Schneider Electric, Eaton, ABB, Hammond Power Solutions, Virginia Transformer, SGB-SMIT, TMC Transformers and Federal Pacific.

Companies are competing through transformer efficiency, manufacturing capacity, product reliability, harmonic mitigation, digital monitoring and technical support. Suppliers offering customized dry-type transformer solutions and dependable delivery capabilities are positioned to address the requirements of expanding hyperscale and colocation facilities.
